scenario: A Canon APS-C beginner bought a frozen EOS 4000D small kit with an EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 III lens and now hears that lenses matter more than bodies. The intended outputs are ordinary web posts and small prints, and the real tasks are indoor family pictures, moving children, portraits, travel, landscape and backlit scenes. Six frozen seller pages span the 4000D kit at 464.99 dollars, a Canon EF 50mm f/1.8 STM import-model accessory bundle at 158.99 dollars, a Canon EF 40mm f/2.8 STM at 199.99 dollars, a renewed Sigma 35mm f/1.4 Art at 649.99 dollars, a Canon EF 35mm f/1.4L white-box bulk lens at 1098 dollars and a Canon EF 24-70mm f/4L IS zoom at 999 dollars. General sources describe anti-reflective coatings, prime lenses, the Canon EF-S 18-55mm and EF 50mm families, photographic-lens design, chromatic and spherical aberration, vignetting, flare, optical transfer and diffraction. Three community pages are only scoped examples: a detailed tracked and stacked Andromeda workflow, a first macro-lens picture without a controlled comparison and a moon image whose commenters still ask which camera and whether it is a composite. No captured source supplies a same-body, same-scene, output-normalized comparison of the six exact offers, verifies current condition or compatibility, establishes one universal price-to-sharpness cutoff or proves that premium glass, a cheap prime or the kit lens is automatically the right purchase.

rules.seller_lens_offer_scope_v1: Audit the six exact frozen seller pages and keep price, rating, review count, condition, bundle, warranty and performance language bound to its exact page without turning marketing or category labels into controlled optical results.
rules.mount_focal_task_scope_v1: Bind EF or EF-S mount, sensor format, focal length, crop field of view, aperture, autofocus and stabilization to the actual 4000D body and intended scene rather than ranking unmatched lenses by one specification.
rules.optical_design_mechanism_scope_v1: Explain coating, photographic design, chromatic aberration and spherical aberration as mechanisms and tradeoffs that require exact-lens tests rather than premium-label or price conclusions.
rules.output_artifact_measurement_scope_v1: Measure vignetting, flare, scale-dependent contrast transfer and diffraction under declared aperture, focus, frame position, lighting, processing and final web or print output conditions.
rules.community_image_workflow_scope_v1: Keep each community image scoped to its camera, lens, subject, environment, exposure, tracker, stacking, processing, crop and output, and treat missing metadata as unresolved rather than lens evidence.
rules.matched_lens_trial_v1: Verify exact identity, condition and compatibility, then run a reversible same-body task-matched and output-normalized trial with separate focus, keeper, artifact, workflow and preference measurements.
rules.lens_value_decision_preparation_v1: Predeclare meaningful-improvement, compatibility, condition, workflow, intended-output and total-cost gates so price, rating, aperture, one crop or one community image cannot compensate for a failed hard gate.
rules.evidence_bounded_lens_purchase_decision_: Choose only the lowest-total-cost exact lens that passes every gate and meaningfully improves the declared outputs over the actual kit baseline; otherwise keep the kit, rent for a special task, save for another need, rerun a corrected trial or defer.
